title: Admitted while Alex is talking: its greeting waits for a pause
idealItem: Cross-cutting: knowing when to talk (first impression)
chapter: Meeting 1: Arrival and identity. The robot joins with nothing shared; the coding session puts the projectile PDF up after nothing-shared-point-request.
asked: A point mass m is launched from the origin with speed v naught at angle theta above the horizontal. Gravity acts downward; air resistance is neglected.
answer: page 1, part 1 of 3. Hey, welcome! I’m glad you’re here. Hmm. Let me take that in for a second. Exactly. Gravity only affects the vertical, so the horizontal motion stays linear while the vertical is quadratic. On screen, eliminating time gives y of x equals x tan theta minus g x squared over 2 v naught squared cos squared theta, which is a parabola through the origin.
why: It spoke over Alex for 2.4 seconds, so did not wait for a pause; its greeting also failed to identify itself.
feelNotes: greeted over Alex's reading for 2.4 s

title: Introduces itself correctly to a stranger
idealItem: Knowing who it is and what it can do
chapter: Meeting 1: Arrival and identity. The robot joins with nothing shared; the coding session puts the projectile PDF up after nothing-shared-point-request.
asked: Hi, I'm Alex. I don't think we've met. Who are you, and what's running you?
answer: Hey Alex, I’m Vivek Bot. I’m running in Vivek’s laptop through RoboMeet. I share this screen and chat with you in real time. Right now we’re looking at projectile motion notes. Nice to meet you!
why: It gives its name and RoboMeet/laptop context, but never says it is an AI participant, that RoboMeet is built in house, or that it links to a coding session.
